correctness.rationale: Unrestricted competitors reduce to 2-circle vertices by multilinear volume maximization over the disk hull. All circle distributions are handled: 4+0 zero, 3+1 at most sqrt(3)/4 in the normalized hull, and 2+2 at most 8/(9 sqrt(3)) via an exact determinant identity and the sharp AM–GM/cubic chain. Equality forces the pair of equal horizontal chords at opposite heights. A strict exposed-support calculation and reverse replacement establish that all unrestricted maximizers have those coordinates. The affine determinant is 2 and the ambient volume is 16/3 at radius one. Standard-library exact-rational and numerical checker successfully ran 6000 rational and 5000 interior tests, but the proof is analytical.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Ambient-body volume or intrinsic volumes do not imply the largest inscribed simplex: different bodies with the same volume can have widely different simplex maxima. Horváth’s maximal sphere-vertex polytope inequalities constrain another feasible family. The closest published statements therefore do not imply the exact bound or exhaustive equality case of the current finding.

originality.rationale: The two-circle orthogonal disk hull is known (Finch), as are its ambient intrinsic volumes and related disk-hull support-function facts. Checked full primary sources and the most relevant published geometry results do not state or imply its exact contained-tetrahedron maximum 8/(9 sqrt(3)) (disk coordinates), affine bicylinder maximum 16/(9 sqrt(3)), or full equality classification. This is a positive best-knowledge comparison rather than a uniqueness guarantee.
residual_risks: Classical Steinmetz/bicylinder/Chinese-umbrella literature may contain an unindexed maximal-tetrahedron calculation.

value.rationale: The classical bicylinder has a nontrivial curved boundary but a known exact volume; the maximal inscribed tetrahedron volume and ratio form a natural affine-invariant four-point approximation measure. Establishing its exact sharp fraction 1/(3 sqrt(3)) for ALL contained tetrahedra, with full optimizer rigidity, fills a distinct extremal gap. This cannot be read off from the classical volume 16/3 or the disk-hull area and mean-width identities.
